name: Powering AI data centers: on site generation, batteries and the orbital bet
title: Powering AI data centers: on site generation, batteries and the orbital bet
answer: AI data centers are running out of grid. Connections in the busiest markets can take five years or more, so the fastest builders now bring their own power: gas generation on or beside the site, large batteries to smooth the load, and, as a longer bet, computing in orbit powered by sunlight. xAI is the clearest example of the first two and SpaceX of the third.

sources.title: Colossus 1 and 2, behind the meter report (Cleanview)

sections.body: A large AI campus asks a utility for hundreds of megawatts to more than a gigawatt, the output of a power plant. Utilities have to study, approve and often build new transmission before they can serve that, and in markets such as PJM and Northern Virginia the wait runs past five years. Builders who will not wait move behind the meter, generating and storing power on their own land and using the grid as a partial supply or not at all.
sections.heading: Why the grid is the bottleneck

sections.body: xAI built Colossus 1 in Memphis in about four months by powering it largely from its own equipment. Mobile methane gas turbines on the site drew a challenge from the Southern Environmental Law Center and local residents, who said 26 or more turbines ran without the required air permits; reporting has counted as many as 35 at points. For Colossus 2, xAI generates power at the Southaven Power Plant site across the Mississippi line and sends it to the data center buildings over medium voltage lines, with a grid connection serving Colossus 1 only. The approach traded speed for local controversy over air quality and permitting, and it is now being copied by other large builders.
sections.heading: On site generation: the xAI model

sections.body: On site gas generation needs turbines, and turbines are scarce. GE Vernova, one of the main makers, has said it is mostly sold out through 2030, largely because of AI data center demand. The tightest step is casting the blades and vanes for the hottest part of the turbine, which run hotter than the melting point of the alloy they are made from and must each be grown as a single crystal in a vacuum furnace; only four companies worldwide do this at industrial scale. On 29 August 2026 Elon Musk confirmed that SpaceX is building its own blades and vanes foundry in Bastrop, Texas, on roughly 830 acres it bought near its Starlink factory, saying in house casting could bring natural gas turbines online up to 18 months sooner. The foundry is a SpaceX project; Tesla's part in Musk's energy plans is solar and battery manufacturing, which he said both companies are expanding. The catch is that faster turbines mean more gas burned near homes: in Memphis the NAACP has accused the company of running turbines without the required permits and pollution controls.
sections.heading: Making the turbines: the SpaceX foundry

sections.body: Between the generators, the grid and the GPUs sit batteries. They absorb the sharp swings in demand that training runs create, carry the site through outages, and in xAI's case were a condition of getting grid service. The site's full treatment is on the Tesla Megapack page.
sections.heading: Batteries in the middle

sections.body: SpaceX, which acquired xAI in February 2026, says it will launch its first AI computing satellite in the fourth quarter of 2027, built around a space version of Nvidia's Vera Rubin system, with significant scale in 2028, and it has applied to the Federal Communications Commission to operate up to one million data center satellites. Google's Project Suncatcher plans two test satellites carrying its AI chips in 2027 with Planet Labs, and Blue Origin has filed for 51,600 data center satellites. The appeal is constant sunlight and no grid queue. The obstacles are physical and economic: in a vacuum the chips' heat can only leave as infrared radiation, which needs very large radiators; commercial AI chips are not radiation hardened; links to the ground limit bandwidth; nothing can be repaired by hand; and ABI Research has estimated an orbital data center could cost more than 78 times a comparable facility on the ground. Treat the 2027 dates as test milestones, not proof of commercial scale.
sections.heading: The orbital bet

sections.body: Behind the meter generation moves the fight from the utility commission to the air permit office, as Memphis showed. Batteries ease the load on the grid but do not remove it. And orbital computing, if it ever scales, would move the energy question off the ground entirely while raising new ones about launch emissions, orbital debris and spectrum. The site tracks the bills and siting rules on its data center siting and power page.
